name: Zohar
overview: Zohar was a male member of the Hittite tribe known primarily as the father of Ephron, who sold the cave at Machpelah to Abraham. His role is briefly mentioned in the context of this significant transaction recorded in Genesis. Beyond this, there are no additional notes or details about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Zohar means "yellowish red" or "tawny," reflecting a descriptive Hebrew proper name. It is not indicated that this name was given by God but is simply a personal identifier in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Zohar as the father of Ephron, who is notable for selling the burial cave to Abraham. He is also recognized as a descendant of Heth, linking him to the Hittite lineage. No other family relationships are recorded beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Zohar's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his son Ephron's role in the purchase of the cave at Machpelah, which became Abraham's burial site. This transaction represents an important moment in the patriarchal history, marking the first piece of promised land acquired by Abraham. Through Zohar's familial link, the narrative situates the Hittites as key participants in God's unfolding plan for His people.
